verdict.root_cause: Cart cache round trips are uniformly slow and the wait, not any error inside cartservice, is what breaks a slice of frontend requests. Traces show cartservice server spans spending essentially all their time in Redis client spans (HGET/HMSET ~300-306ms each, only ~1-3ms of in-process overhead), while every other downstream in the same traces stays under ~20ms; the delay propagates to frontend GetCart ~304-308ms, frontend AddItem ~909-919ms and checkoutservice PlaceOrder ~635-649ms. Frontend's error ratio stepped off an exactly-zero baseline at 15:13:45Z to ~2.8% mean / ~12% peak, the shape of timeout-driven partial failure rather than a hard break, and both cartservice and checkoutservice keep logging successful operations through the window close. The quantized ~300ms-per-operation signature matches the 300ms eth0 egress delay platform-automation repeatedly attached to cartservice in this environment, so the live mechanism is most likely injected/residual network delay on cartservice's path to its Redis cache.
verdict.reasoning: Latency is localized below cartservice: caller spans exceed callee spans by ~1-4ms and callee spans exceed their Redis children by ~1-3ms, ruling out frontend handler, network-to-cartservice, and cartservice CPU [tr_e24f457d6c26]. Other downstreams are fast in the same traces, so this is not a mesh-wide or shared-dependency slowdown [tr_e24f457d6c26]. Frontend errors are new and step-onset, consistent with a discrete trigger plus deadline breaches on the slowest cart-dependent requests [tr_f278917582f6]. cartservice's own logs and metrics show no errors, crashes, or connection failures, so it is failing slow, not failing hard [tr_ba01bf74b285][tr_e24f457d6c26]. The uniform, non-long-tailed ~300ms quantum matches the recorded 300ms egress-delay injection on cartservice rather than organic cache load [tr_adda4309014f].
open_questions: Whether the traffic-shaping container is actually absent from the cartservice pod now; the change log's removal claim is untrusted and no dispatch observed live network state.
Traces carried no timestamps or status codes and were truncated at 200 spans, so the slow spans cannot be pinned to the 15:13-15:36 sub-window or tied to specific errored requests.
Redis-cart itself was never queried directly (latency, CPU, connections), so a slow cache backend rather than injected path delay is not excluded.
Both log queries elided the middle of the window, including 15:13-15:35, so the onset moment was never directly observed.

alternatives.root_cause: The redis-cart backend itself became slow (saturation or its own resource pressure), making cartservice wait ~300ms per operation.
alternatives.why_not: Redis-side saturation typically produces a long latency tail, not the tight ~300ms/~600ms quantization seen in traces, and no dispatch measured redis-cart directly.

alternatives.root_cause: A REDIS_ADDR override left cartservice pointed at a wrong or misrouted cache endpoint, adding fixed delay to every cache call.
alternatives.why_not: The change log reports every REDIS_ADDR override reverted to unset ~4.9h before onset, and a wrong address would more likely yield connection errors than uniformly successful 300ms operations.
